flashcards.q: How does Cloud Run autoscale instances?
flashcards.a: instances = ceil(in-flight requests / concurrency), floored by min-instances, capped by max-instances. In-flight follows Little's Law (rps x latency). At the cap with full slots: queue briefly, then HTTP 429.
Default 80 per instance; new services deployed via gcloud CLI/Terraform default to 80 x vCPU. Configurable up to 1000 concurrent requests per instance.
300s default, up to 3600s (60 min) for HTTP-triggered. Eventarc/event-driven functions cap at 9 minutes.

flashcards.q: Two CPU allocation modes and when each applies?
flashcards.a: Default: CPU allocated only while a request is in flight (throttled between requests) - cheapest for pure request/response. Always-allocated (--no-cpu-throttling): required for background threads/polling/cache warming, bills continuously.

On by default for new services: temporarily allocates extra vCPU (~2x) during container startup plus roughly the first 10 seconds to cut cold-start time. Affects startup only, not between-request work.

flashcards.q: What happened to Cloud Functions in Aug 2024?
flashcards.a: 2nd gen renamed Cloud Run functions - deploys as a real Cloud Run service (run.app URL) built by buildpacks from source. Gen1 became 'Cloud Run functions (1st gen)': concurrency 1, 9-min cap, cloudfunctions.net URLs, supported but legacy.

Gen2: concurrency up to 1000/instance, HTTP timeout to 60 min, up to 16 GiB / 4 vCPU shapes, 90+ Eventarc sources, traffic splitting, CloudEvents. Gen1: concurrency 1, 9-min timeout, 8 GiB / 2 vCPU, 7 direct triggers.
Pub/Sub-backed, at-least-once, unordered by default, configurable retries with dead-letter topics. Handlers must be idempotent (dedup on CloudEvent id); monitor DLQ as first-class signal.

flashcards.q: Direct events vs audit-log events - key difference?
flashcards.a: Direct events are structured service events (GCS object finalized, Pub/Sub message). Audit-log events wrap google.cloud.audit.log.v1.written for nearly any service and support resourceName PATH PATTERNS - the only way to prefix-filter GCS triggers.

flashcards.q: Most common reason a trigger deploys but never fires?
flashcards.a: The trigger's service account lacks roles/run.invoker on the target Cloud Run service - trigger creates successfully and silently never delivers. Also check region alignment between trigger and target.

flashcards.q: When does Cloud Run lose to GKE economically?
flashcards.a: Flat sustained load: always-on instance-seconds approach or exceed small committed-use clusters consolidating multiple workloads. Spiky/idle-heavy traffic favors Cloud Run; compute monthly vCPU-seconds both ways.

flashcards.q: Private VPC egress options and current preference?
flashcards.a: Direct VPC egress routes outbound through a chosen subnet (private IPs + Cloud NAT for fixed egress IP) - preferred. Serverless VPC Access connector is the older hop-by-proxy path with throughput ceilings and its own billing.

flashcards.q: Standard vs flexible environment in one line each?
flashcards.a: Standard: sandboxed managed runtimes, scales to zero, cheap, no arbitrary binaries. Flexible: dockerized on GCE VMs, never scales to zero. Greenfield default is Cloud Run either way.
